title: One Farmers Market board for the screen and the table (after the board look is chosen)
problem: The market is a grid of flat cells and the lorry is a smoothed picture; the owner wants the board to look the same in the game and on a real table (DEC-033).
scope: First the owner chooses the board look (DEC-034); the rest of the game is then designed back from it
Board sprites and art in the chosen look
Screen market rebuilt as slots with printed prices, keeping buy taps and animation anchors
A printable board and token set generated from the same game data (the A3 prototype is one candidate look)
RULES.md "Playing on a table": the board and how nights are handled
exclusions: Skins for the other league stages

acceptance.text: Screen and printed mat are generated from the same slot data (test compares track lengths and prices with the game data)
acceptance.evidence: Printed prototype only: the A3 mat and tokens are generated from the game data (track lengths 3, 6, 7, 6; prices from the cost table). The screen market is not rebuilt yet, so the comparison cannot run.

acceptance.text: Buying, putting back and the animations work as before on the new market (unit and browser tests)
The mat prints on A3 at 100% with all four tracks legible
acceptance.evidence: Prototype made (Board_Prototype_A3.html and .pdf: one A3 landscape page and three A4 pages checked in a PDF render). Not printed on paper yet.

acceptance.text: A hand-played table game with the mat
acceptance.evidence: Needs people and the printed set

acceptance.text: The new market looks right and is easy to tap on a phone
Lint, types, unit tests, build and browser tests pass
